response_text:
Great — this is a really fun route for spring break. Below is a workable, family-friendly plan (cars, hotels, day‑by‑day, driving, budget and practical tips) that keeps your dates and $3,000 total budget in mind. I give a “recommended/comfy” option and a “budget-savvy” alternative where helpful so you can decide what to book.

Quick summary / travel skeleton
- Fly into SAT (arrive afternoon Apr 10) → pick up rental car at SAT.
- San Antonio stay: Apr 10–13 (3 nights).
- Drive SAT → Austin Apr 13 (~1.5 hr).
- Austin stay: Apr 13–17 (4 nights).
- Drive Austin → Houston Apr 17 (~2.5–3 hr). Drop car at HOU (recommended because your return flight is HOU → SEA on Apr 18 morning). Optionally drop at IAH but that’s farther from HOU and usually unnecessary.
- Return flight HOU → SEA on Apr 18 morning.

1) Rental car — recommendation + costs + tips
Recommended category
- Compact or mid-size SUV (e.g., Toyota RAV4, Honda CR‑V, Nissan Rogue) — big enough for 4 people + 2 small/medium suitcases + 2 car seats/boosters, comfortable for longer drives, better visibility and more cargo room than a sedan.

Why: family comfort, room for luggage and souvenirs, easier with child seats. If you’re prioritizing cost over space, a mid-size sedan will save you money but with tighter trunk space.

Estimated cost for 7–8 days (pickup SAT / drop HOU)
- Typical range: $450–$800 total (depends on company, one‑way fee, demand).
- Good working estimate to use in your budget: $550–$650 (includes a moderate one‑way drop fee).
- One‑way drop fees can vary widely ($100–$300). Compare companies and look for offers with lower one‑way charges.

Tips for best rental deals for this route
- Book early (rates rise fast for spring break / events).
- Compare aggregators (Kayak, Expedia, Rentalcars.com) and then go to the rental company site — sometimes direct rates are better.
- Check Costco Travel, AAA, or your credit‑card rental discounts — they can reduce rates and include insurance perks.
- Look for “no prepay” free cancellation options so you can rebook if prices fall.
- Ask about including one additional driver (sometimes free if spouse is on same reservation).
- Bring your own boosters/car seats if possible — rental child seats are $10–$15/day each and add up.
- Check credit‑card collision damage waiver (CDW) coverage before buying extra insurance.
- Inspect car thoroughly and photograph damage on pickup and return.

2) Hotel picks (family-friendly, near Riverwalk and walkable to SoCo/downtown)
San Antonio — 3 nights (Apr 10–13). Focus: Riverwalk area (close to attractions and easy walking)

Top picks (2–3 options)
1. Drury Plaza Hotel San Antonio Riverwalk
- Approx price/night: $150–$240 (varies by date)
- Pros: Free hot breakfast and evening “Kickback” (huge family value), indoor/outdoor pool, suites available, direct Riverwalk access.
- Cons: Can fill up fast during events; downtown parking fees.
- Good for families because breakfast + evening snacks reduce food spend and pool entertains kids after travel.

2. Hotel Contessa (on the Riverwalk, all‑suite)
- Approx price/night: $200–$320
- Pros: Spacious suites with living area/kitchenette, riverfront location, upscale.
- Cons: Pricier; parking fee.
- Good for families who want extra space and kitchenette to rehearse meals / store snacks.

3. Hyatt Regency San Antonio Riverwalk (or Omni La Mansión del Rio)
- Approx price/night: $200–$300
- Pros: Very central; large hotel amenities; pool; easy access to Riverwalk boat tours.
- Cons: Higher nightly rates; parking fees.

Budget alternative
- Holiday Inn Express / Hampton Inn downtown or a well-rated downtown Best Western: ~$110–$160/night. Less luxurious but often includes breakfast.

Austin — 4 nights (Apr 13–17). Preference: walkable to South Congress (SoCo) or downtown

Top picks (2–3 options)
1. South Congress Hotel (SoCo)
- Approx price/night: $300–$450
- Pros: Iconic SoCo location — walk to shops/restaurants; boutique vibe.
- Cons: Higher price; limited kid‑specific amenities.
- Best if you want to be in the center of SoCo activity.

2. Hotel San Jose (on SoCo) or Austin Motel (SoCo)
- Approx price/night: $200–$300
- Pros: Walkable, quirky boutique, great for exploring SoCo on foot, casual atmosphere.
- Cons: Smaller rooms; limited on‑site amenities (pool season permitting).

3. Hyatt Regency / The LINE Austin (downtown / riverfront)
- Approx price/night: $200–$325
- Pros: Riverfront access (great for kayaking/bat-watching), big hotel amenities (pool), walkable to downtown and not too far from SoCo.
- Cons: Can be busy; parking fees.

Budget alternative
- Holiday Inn Express or Hampton Inn Austin Downtown / South (within 1–2 miles of SoCo): $140–$200/night. Good free breakfast, basic family rooms.

Note about parking & fees
- Many downtown hotels charge $20–$40/night for self/valet parking — include that in your calculations. Look for hotels with free parking or free breakfast to save.

3) Day‑by‑day itinerary (kid-friendly pacing for ages 8 & 11)

San Antonio
April 10 (arrival afternoon)
- Pick up car at SAT (plan 45–75 minutes after disembark).
- Check into Riverwalk hotel.
- Kid‑friendly, low‑effort options: quick dip in hotel pool (best if you choose hotel with pool), a short gentle stroll along the River Walk, casual dinner on the riverside (lots of family options).
- If energy allows and you want quick sightseeing: 30–40 min River Walk boat tour (relaxing for kids after a flight).
- Early night so kids adjust to time and recover.

April 11 (full day — hands-on + fun)
- Morning: The DoSeum (San Antonio’s children’s museum) — interactive exhibits for hands‑on STEM play (2–3 hours).
- Lunch: Pearl District or Riverwalk kid-friendly spots.
- Afternoon: San Antonio Zoo and Brackenridge Park OR Witte Museum (natural history + interactive exhibits) — choose zoo if kids love animals.
- Evening: Dinner on the Riverwalk; optional ride up Tower of the Americas for a city view if energy remains.

April 12 (full day — adventure)
- Option A (adventure & animals): Natural Bridge Caverns (guided cave tour) + Natural Bridge Wildlife Ranch drive‑thru safari. Both are north of the city near New Braunfels — great for kids.
- Option B (theme park): SeaWorld San Antonio OR Six Flags Fiesta Texas (check seasonal openings).
- Evening: Relax at hotel; let kids swim or you can explore La Villita historic district.

April 13 (morning before checkout)
- Quick morning: Short River Walk boat tour or quick visit to The Alamo (15–30 minute visit) — keep it short for kids.
- Drive SAT → Austin (I‑35 N) mid/late morning. Stop suggestions on route: New Braunfels or San Marcos outlets for a stretch/lunch.

Austin
April 13 (arrive afternoon/evening)
- Check into SoCo or downtown hotel.
- First evening: Walk South Congress (shops, tacos, ice cream). Early dinner at a family‑friendly SoCo spot (Home Slice Pizza, Guero’s, Torchy’s).
- If timing works: an early bat-watch option (see bat section) — head to Congress Ave Bridge 30–45 minutes before sunset.

April 14 (full day — museums + outdoors)
- Morning: Thinkery (Austin children’s museum) — hands‑on STEAM exhibits geared to your kids’ ages.
- Lunch: Picnic or food trucks (lots of family choices).
- Afternoon: Zilker Park — Zilker Zephyr train, playgrounds, and if weather is warm, walk around Barton Springs (swim depending on temp).
- Evening: Bat emergence at Congress Ave Bridge at dusk (April is often a good month; go early to secure a spot).

April 15 (full day — city & history)
- Morning: Texas State Capitol tour (free, guided) — short and engaging; kids often like the building scale and grounds.
- Late morning/early afternoon: Bullock Texas State History Museum (IMAX or exhibits) or Blanton Art Museum for kid‑friendly exhibits.
- Afternoon: Rent kayaks or a family canoe on Lady Bird Lake (easy rentals near the boardwalk) or walk the Ann and Roy Butler Hike-and-Bike Trail.
- Evening: SoCo dinner or early dinner in downtown.

April 16 (full day — choose one)
- Option A: Day trip to Hamilton Pool Preserve (reservations required) — beautiful but check reservation windows; best for older kids who enjoy nature hikes (about 45–60 min west of Austin).
- Option B: Inner Space Cavern (Georgetown) or a visit to nearby Pedernales Falls State Park (hiking).
- Option C: Chill day exploring more of SoCo, vintage shops, local parks; or a family activity like Topgolf if everyone wants a more active evening.

April 17 (checkout morning → drive to Houston)
- Early checkout and drive Austin → Houston (I‑10 E — ~2.5–3 hrs).
- Suggested stop en route: Bastrop (historic downtown) or Brenham (Blue Bell Creamery if open — good for kids).
- Arrive Houston; if you want less stress for morning flight, drop car at HOU and stay at a near‑airport hotel (recommended) the night of Apr 17. If you prefer to keep car until morning Apr 18, allow extra time to return to HOU early Apr 18.

4) Top 5 kid‑friendly must‑do activities in each city (ages 8–11)

San Antonio (top 5)
1. The DoSeum — interactive children’s museum (hands‑on science & play).
2. River Walk boat tour — short, relaxing, great orientation and kid‑friendly.
3. Natural Bridge Caverns + drive‑thru Wildlife Ranch — caves + safari fun.
4. San Antonio Zoo — classic family favorite.
5. The Alamo / San Antonio Missions (short, educational visit + mission grounds to explore).

Austin (top 5)
1. Thinkery — premier kids’ museum with age‑appropriate interactive exhibits.
2. Congress Avenue Bridge bat emergence at dusk — memorable experience for kids.
3. Zilker Park + Zilker Zephyr train and Barton Springs area — plenty of play space.
4. Lady Bird Lake kayaking or family paddleboard — active outdoor fun.
5. Texas State Capitol + Bullock Museum — short, kid‑friendly tours about Texas history.

5) Driving routes, times, and recommended stops

SAT → Austin
- Route: I‑35 N direct is fastest and simplest (about 80–85 miles).
- Driving time: ~1.5–2 hours depending on traffic.
- Stops worth making: New Braunfels / Gruene (historic district, river views, great lunch), San Marcos outlets (short stop to stretch).

Austin → Houston (to HOU)
- Route: I‑10 E (most direct).
- Driving time: ~2.5–3 hours depending on traffic.
- Stops: Bastrop (historic downtown), Brenham (Blue Bell Creamery — seasonal hours), Columbus or Sealy for bathrooms/food.
- Fuel stops: Use GasBuddy or plan to stop at big Texas travel plazas (Buc‑ee’s if convenient) for bathrooms and snacks.

Notes on airport drop-off
- Drop at HOU if your flight is from HOU — saves a connection to IAH. One‑way fees apply — compare rental companies.
- Allow an extra 60–90 minutes when returning a car at the airport (drop, return shuttle, TSA).

6) Budget breakdown (estimated)

Estimated (balanced / family of 4) — target total under $3,000:

| Category | Estimated Cost |
|----------|----------------|
| Rental car (7–8 days, compact/mid‑size SUV, one‑way SAT→HOU) | $600 |
| San Antonio hotels (3 nights, mid-range near Riverwalk) | $450 |
| Austin hotels (4 nights, mid-range near SoCo/downtown) | $700 |
| Activities (museum tickets, tours, zoo, caverns, kayak rentals) | $300 |
| Food / dining (mix of breakfasts, lunches, dinners) | $700 |
| Gas (approx. 500–700 miles) | $150 |
| **Total** | **$2,900** |

Notes:
- This plan assumes mid-range nightly hotel averages ($150/night SA; $175/night Austin). If you choose more upscale hotels (South Congress Hotel, Hotel Contessa), add $300–$700.
- Parking fees (downtown hotels) commonly $20–40/night — not included above. If applicable, add ~$140–$280. If you choose hotels with free breakfast and pool (Drury, Holiday Inn Express), you’ll save on food.
- Car‑seat rentals (if needed) can add $10–15/day per seat — consider bringing at least one booster to save money.
- If your rental one-way fee is higher (~$300) or you choose a pricier SUV, adjust the car line accordingly.

How to stay under $3,000
- Choose budget/midrange hotels with free breakfast (Drury, Hampton Inn, Holiday Inn Express).
- Bring at least one car seat/booster; gate‑check car seats on the flight instead of renting at the counter.
- Limit paid activities to 2–3 “must‑do” paid attractions; choose more free/low‑cost things (Zilker Park, Riverwalk, Capitol grounds).
- Use grocery/fast casual for 1–2 dinners.
- Watch for hotel parking fees — choose hotels that include parking if possible.

7) Practical tips (apps, packing, April specifics)

Best apps
- Road planning & navigation: Google Maps, Waze, Roadtrippers (fun stop ideas).
- Fuel: GasBuddy (compare prices, find Buc‑ee’s).
- Kids & car entertainment: Audible, Netflix (download offline shows), Spotify (family playlists), Caribu (interactive reading).
- Local tickets & timing: Reserve on Thinkery, Natural Bridge Caverns, Hamilton Pool (these can require reservations).
- Parking: ParkMobile for city garages.

What to pack in the car (family of 4)
- Two car seats / boosters or plan to rent them. If flying with them, gate‑check options exist.
- Snacks (zip bags), small cooler, refillable water bottles, wet wipes, hand sanitizer.
- Chargers & power bank, headphones for each kid, tablet with downloaded shows/games.
- Basic first aid kit, motion‑sickness medication if needed.
- Lightweight rain jackets/ponchos (spring showers possible), hat & sunscreen.
- Foldable blanket, change of clothes for kids, plastic bags for trash/dirty clothes.
- Printed copies of reservations and IDs.

April‑specific events & notes
- Fiesta San Antonio typically takes place in April (mid‑April). If your trip overlaps Fiesta dates, expect heavier crowds and higher hotel rates in San Antonio — check exact fiesta dates for your year and book ASAP. (This is a big local event with parades, food booths, and increased traffic.)
- April is bluebonnet / wildflower season in central Texas — great for roadside photos (pull over safely).
- Bat season in Austin: by April the Mexican free‑tailed bats are usually emerging nightly from Congress Ave Bridge; emergence times change through the season — go 30–45 minutes before sunset for best viewing.
- Spring break season: expect some crowds at family attractions; reserve timed admission where possible.

Final quick checklist & next steps (action items)
1. Decide rental vehicle size (compact SUV recommended) and check prices for SAT pickup / HOU drop — book early and compare Costco/AAA/credit‑card deals.
2. Pick and reserve hotels (Riverwalk in SA and SoCo or downtown in Austin). If Fiesta overlaps your dates, book now.
3. Reserve any timed tickets: Thinkery, Natural Bridge Caverns, Hamilton Pool (if chosen).
4. Decide on car seats: bring yours (gate‑check) or reserve two from rental (book with rental as add‑on).
5. Build a simple “snacks & entertainment” bag for the car to save on food and keep kids happy.
6. Save contact information for your rental company’s airport return instructions and hotel parking policies.

If you’d like, I can:
- Run 2–3 specific hotel matches and estimated exact nightly rates for your dates (I can give likely price ranges and which nights are busiest).
- Compare 3 rental car quotes (examples of typical cost with major companies) for pickup SAT / drop HOU.
- Make a printable day-by-day with addresses, drive times and reservation links.

Would you like me to find specific hotels and a sample rental quote for your exact travel dates (Apr 10–17/18) so you can book?
